content:
Sean Gallagher: Hey folks — for the KV compaction canary, we need crisp metric defs + initial alert thresholds. Also: what signals tell us “compaction is causing the p99 spike” vs just traffic mix / noisy neighbor.

Allison Grant: +1. Can you list the exact metric names you’re planning to emit (and units), esp fragmentation ratio + compaction time + bytes moved + eviction counters? I want to wire them into the standard dashboard + alert routing.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep. Draft names (all runtime-exported, per instance, with model + pool labels):
- `runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio` (gauge, 0.0–1.0) = 1 - (largest_free_contiguous_bytes / total_free_bytes). Higher = worse fragmentation.
- `runtime_kv_free_bytes` (gauge)
- `runtime_kv_used_bytes` (gauge)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total` (counter)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total` (counter)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_steps_total` (counter)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_stalls_total` (counter) — increments when scheduler had to defer decode due to relocation lock > budget
- `runtime_kv_evictions_total` (counter) + `runtime_kv_evicted_bytes_total` (counter)
- `runtime_kv_eviction_reasons_total{reason=...}` where reason in `pressure_high`, `tier_preempt`, `prefix_cache`, `allocator_health`
- `runtime_scheduler_decode_delay_ms` (histogram) — time decode waited on “memory ops” bucket

Samir Qureshi: One nuance on `fragmentation_ratio`: we’re using arena-level free list view. It doesn’t mean “unusable”, but it correlates with allocation scan cost + forced evictions when big contiguous blocks are needed.

Allison Grant: Thanks. For `runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total` and bytes moved, do we also have a per-interval gauge or histogram? Counters are fine but alerts are easier on rates.

Logan Wright: We can emit rate off the counters in Prom. But we can also add:
- `runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_per_sec` (gauge) computed in-process (EWMA)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_per_sec` (gauge) (also EWMA)
If you prefer no extra metrics, we can keep it to counters + recording rules.

Sean Gallagher: Recording rules are fine. I mainly need: “what is expected range” during canary so we don’t page on normal behavior.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler integration piece: compaction runs at prefill/decode boundary with a budget (time + bytes). When we violate budget, that’s when you’ll see `decode_delay_ms` move + p99 jump. If it’s working correctly, p99 should be flat and you’ll see compaction time spread out.

Rafael Mendes: From oncall POV I need a simple decision tree: p99 up —> check X/Y/Z —> kill-switch or not.

Omar El-Sayed: Suggested “compaction-caused latency spike” signature:
1) `runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_per_sec` spikes AND `runtime_scheduler_decode_delay_ms` p95/p99 spikes in same window.
2) `runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio` is high (e.g. >0.55) and falling after compaction starts.
3) p99 latency spike happens without corresponding QPS spike / token/sec spike.
4) Often see `runtime_kv_compaction_stalls_total` increasing (that should be near-zero in steady state).
If p99 spikes but compaction metrics are flat, it’s probably traffic mix, upstream queuing, or GPU contention.

Sean Gallagher: Can we nail initial thresholds for canary (Hosted small cohort)? I’m thinking 3 tiers:
- warn (Slack)
- page (oncall)
- rollback trigger (automation)

Paula Mendes: For automated rollback, we typically require 2 consecutive 5m windows, and we gate on p99 + error rate. We can add compaction metrics as “attribution signals” but the rollback should be based on user-impacting KPIs.

Allison Grant: Agree. But we can still page earlier if compaction is running away before users feel it.

Samir Qureshi: Proposals (rough, based on lab runs):
- `runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio` WARN if >0.60 for 10m (means allocator health is degrading)
- PAGE if >0.75 for 10m AND `runtime_kv_evictions_total` rate > baseline (means we’re thrashing)
- Compaction overhead WARN if `rate(runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total[5m]) > 250ms/s` (i.e. >25% of a core-second equivalent per second) on >30% of instances in pool
- PAGE if `rate(... ) > 500ms/s` and decode_delay p99 increases >20% from baseline

Sean Gallagher: “250ms/s” is a bit abstract for folks. Can we express as “compaction CPU time” or “% time in compaction”?

Caleb Johnson: We can map it as fraction of wall time via recording rule: `compaction_time_fraction = rate(compaction_time_ms_total[5m]) / 1000`. Then 0.25 = 25%.

Allison Grant: Perfect. Then:
- WARN at >0.15 (15%)
- PAGE at >0.30 (30%)
Does that align with safe budgets?

Sofia Ivanova: Yes. Budget is set so we should be <10% most of the time. If we’re >30% it’s likely we’re compaction-chasing fragmentation, which is exactly what we want to catch.

Rafael Mendes: What about eviction alerts? Eviction itself might be OK (tier-aware), but it can hurt customers if it starts hitting pinned sessions.

Omar El-Sayed: We won’t evict pinned sessions; pinned will be “allocation fails” instead (backpressure). But eviction rate is still a signal:
- WARN if `rate(runtime_kv_evictions_total[5m])` > (baseline + 2x) AND `fragmentation_ratio` >0.65
- PAGE if eviction reason `pressure_high` dominates AND p99 latency up >15%.

Sean Gallagher: For rollback automation: propose:
- Rollback if API p99 (end-to-end) for canary cohort > baseline + 20% for 2x 5m windows OR 5xx rate > baseline + 0.2% absolute.
- Add “compaction attribution” annotation if `compaction_time_fraction > 0.20` OR `decode_delay_ms` p99 > baseline + 25%.
Thoughts?

Paula Mendes: Works. We’ll implement rollback trigger off p99 + 5xx; the attribution signals just go into the incident summary + Slack message.

Allison Grant: Metric labels: please make sure we have at least `{pool, model, tier}` and ideally `{gpu_type}`. Otherwise dashboards get messy.

Logan Wright: `pool`, `model`, `tier` yes. `gpu_type` comes from node label; should be joinable but not always present in runtime metrics. We can add it at scrape relabel if needed.

Sean Gallagher: Last ask: if compaction is misbehaving, what should oncall flip first? (Kill-switch vs reduce budget vs disable eviction)

Samir Qureshi: Suggested order:
1) Reduce compaction budget (time + bytes) by 50% (should cut decode impact immediately)
2) If still spiking, disable compaction (kill-switch) but leave eviction on (eviction is safer than OOM)
3) If eviction is causing customer-visible issues (rare), dial eviction threshold up (less aggressive) — but watch for OOM / request shedding

Rafael Mendes: Great, that’s the runbook chunk I needed.

Allison Grant: I’ll draft the dashboard panels: fragmentation ratio over time, compaction time fraction, bytes moved rate, eviction rate by reason, decode_delay_ms, and overlay API p99. Will share a link once it’s in staging.

Sean Gallagher: Awesome. Omar/Samir can you sanity check the definitions in the dashboard once Allison posts? Want to avoid “ratio is inverted” type bugs.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep, we’ll review. Also I’ll drop the exact PromQL snippets for the recording rules in-thread later today.

Caleb Johnson: If you want exemplar traces: we can attach trace IDs when `compaction_stalls_total` increments (span event). That makes “this p99 spike was compaction” super obvious.

Sofia Ivanova: +1, we already have a span around relocation; adding an exemplar event on stall is easy.

Sean Gallagher: Cool — shipping that would help a lot during canary.

Allison Grant: Please do. It’ll reduce finger-pointing :)

Samir Qureshi: lol. ok I’ll open a small follow-up PR for stall exemplars.

Paula Mendes: Once thresholds are finalized, ping me and I’ll update the rollout policy template for runtime-1.22 canary.
